mappings.note: Explicit two-part item: the statement half is LO-6, the unit-definition half is LO-7's tail clause. Both are demanded by the stem, so both are cited.
Statement of the first law (LO-5) plus the reason the ancient misconception survived - friction disguises the law (LO-63). The misconception half is what pulls friction in as graded content.
The rebuttal is that the applied force goes entirely into cancelling friction (LO-63), leaving the first law intact (LO-5). LO-63 leads because the friction insight is what is being graded.
Definition and attribution of inertia, both inside LO-5's state-and-explain scope.

Static friction rising to match the push (LO-63) so the forces balance and nothing moves (LO-62). No number, so not LO-7 - contrast O23, where the push exceeds friction and an acceleration is computed.

Weight against the normal force, balanced. A free-body inventory, which is LO-62; nothing is inferred from motion so not LO-64, and the normal force is not treated as a third-law partner here so not LO-8 (contrast C191, which does exactly that).
Both proportionalities stated qualitatively. No value is computed, so LO-6 and not LO-7, and no graph or model is built, so no C8.1.
Long-form version of the catching item; same outcome pair as O14, O21 and V81.
The third-law premise is given in the stem and a = F/m supplies the answer. Same as O41 and O44 in extended-response form.
A systematic comparison on magnitude, direction and effect on motion - LO-62 for the classification, LO-64 for the effect column.

Weight must be computed as mg, and C2.2 is the only code covering weight; the upward force is then set by balance (LO-62); the 30 x 9.8 arithmetic is LO-7. P1 poses the same scenario without numbers and takes LO-62 alone, which is the split.
Two values are produced (LO-7) with the third law supplying the equal force on the gun (LO-8). Same pair as O32.
Everyday safety device explained by a longer stopping time; same pair as the rest of the cushioning family.
Friction subtracted from the applied force, then F = ma. Numerically a near-twin of O23 and mapped identically rather than split on the numbers.
Renu's misconception is resolved by noting the pair acts on two bodies, so only forces on one body enter its net force (LO-62). Extended-response twin of O27.
Reaction propulsion in a classroom demonstration. The diagram called for is a free-body sketch, not a graph, so no C8.1.
Inverse mass-acceleration comparison plus naming the law. Qualitative, so LO-6 and not LO-7 - contrast L155 and L171, which settle the same kind of comparison by computing both forces.
Extended-response twin of N3: block P from unequal opposing forces (LO-62), block Q from constant velocity (LO-64).
Statement of the third law plus an everyday application, both explicitly demanded by the stem.

The stem asks specifically about interacting forces, so the foot-ground third-law pairing is graded content (LO-8) on top of the low friction (LO-63). Its short-answer twin V87 does not ask that and so trades LO-8 for LO-65.
The cancellation is explicitly justified by the third law (LO-8) and the decision about which forces enter the system's net force is LO-62. The frame has no systems outcome to cite instead.
Weight against buoyancy, balanced. Same as V94; buoyancy is unhoused and weight is reachable only through C2.2.
The graph is drawn (C8.1) and its slope then feeds F = ma (LO-7). Items that read a supplied graph, N11 and O49, take C2.1 instead.
Why the single-system idealisation works and how it simplifies the algebra; symbolic, so LO-6, with C8.1 for the model itself. Same treatment as O36.

The mirror image of the cushioning family - a very short stopping time makes the force large enough to crack the shell. Same outcome pair, applied in the destructive rather than the protective direction.
